space.$description: Spacing scale on a 4px grid; keys are the pixel value.

control.$description: Interactive control heights. Recipes consume these through the density.* semantic aliases (never directly), so the user density axis can shift the whole ladder; xs exists as the compact floor for sm controls (still a workable pointer target beside 15-16px text).

focus-ring.$description: Focus-ring outline geometry — mode-invariant lengths consumed directly by recipes (the focus-ring COLOR is the semantic focus.ring token). Tokenized so components.css carries no literal lengths (design-system area CLAUDE.md: focus-ring width/offset must become tokens before the Tier 1 Button lands).

border-width.$description: Border widths — mode-invariant lengths consumed directly by recipes (the border COLOR is the semantic border.* token). Design language §6: structure is 1px hairline rules and surface tints, shadow reserved for floating layers. Tokenized so components.css carries no literal lengths, exactly as focus-ring width/offset were before the Tier 1 control recipes (Input, Card, Separator, ...) landed.

size.$description: Named layout dimensions for app-shell chrome — mode-invariant, consumed directly by recipes (like control/focus-ring/border-width). The global sidebar (page-archetypes Layout A) is a fixed-width rail that collapses to an icon rail; its two widths are tokens so the mc-sidebar recipe carries no literal length.

top-bar.$description: The chrome band's row height — the TopBar AND the sidebar's brand corner (their edges meet as one band). Taller than a control row: the chrome needs presence and the palette trigger needs air (owner review 2026-07-02). Density-invariant: the frame is layout identity.

transfer-pace.$description: The room a transfer's pace line holds beside its progress bar — "1.2 GB of 4.5 GB · 2.4 MB/s · about 20 min left". Every figure in that line changes length as the transfer runs, so a line sized to its own text resizes the bar beside it several times a second; the measure is fixed, and the bar is what holds still. Sized to the longest line the phrasing produces at the small text size, the way size.create-control is sized to its longest label.

create-control.$description: The one create control, fixed at the width its longest label needs ("New Template" plus the plus glyph and the button's own padding, measured in the reading face at the small size). Fixed rather than fitted so the control never changes width as the reader moves between screens: a label that grows shoves the search beside it, and the search is a control a member reaches for by position. It was 136px while "New Message" was the longest label; the template library needed one character more than that held, and the budget in create-label.ts moves with this value.

prose.$description: The constrained readable measure for descriptions and form bodies (the design language's field discipline: forms and prose are never full-width).

record-window.$description: How wide a record opens before it stops growing. Wider than a reading measure on purpose: the left pane stops at size.record-pane and everything past that goes to the tabs beside it, which is room that side can actually use. The expanded state deliberately ignores this — that is what expanding is for.

record-pane.$description: How wide the record itself gets — the left pane of the record window, and the point past which it stops. Wider than size.prose because this pane carries rows of fields as well as running text, and a three-column field row needs more room than a paragraph does; narrower than the window, because a description set across a wide monitor is harder to read, not easier. Growth past this belongs to the pane beside it.

record-form.$description: How wide the record's own pane gets when it carries the section rail down its left side, as New Person and the record window do: size.record-pane for the fields plus the rail beside them (11rem and its 16px gap). Without the extra the rail is paid for out of the fields, and a three-column name row is squeezed into the width of two.

record-context.$description: How wide the record window's right pane asks to be — the tabs standing beside the record. It is a starting width rather than a cap: attachments, history and the chain each read better with room, so this side is the one that takes whatever width is left once the record has stopped at size.record-pane. While the window is too narrow for both, this width is what decides the two panes' share of it.

record-aside.$description: How wide the record window's side panel stands when a kind of record has one: a conversation that stays in view beside the record and its tabs rather than hiding behind a tab. Fixed rather than flexible, because a running thread reads at a column's width and gains nothing from more, and narrower than size.record-context so the tabs keep the larger share of the spare width.

record-window-wide.$description: How wide a record window with a side panel opens before it stops growing: size.record-window plus size.record-aside, so the panel is added beside the record and its tabs rather than paid for out of them. The expanded state ignores this, as it ignores size.record-window.

modal-gutter.$description: The least of the screen that shows around a windowed modal on every side. A panel that touches the edge stops reading as a panel over the application and starts reading as a page the application was replaced by, with the panel's own rounded corners cut off against the screen. The gutter is what a panel's caps are measured inside: a panel's width cap and its content decide how big it opens, and this decides how big it can ever be on the screen it is on, so on a laptop a long record scrolls inside a window with air around it rather than running from the top of the screen to the bottom. Fixed rather than a share of the screen because a share swells on a large monitor, where the width caps already leave room, and shrinks on a small one, where the air is needed most (owner ruling 2026-09-03, over a proportional gutter). Expanding drops it: filling the screen is that gesture.
